content: _Mycoplasma pneumoniae_ is a type of bacteria that can cause infections in the respiratory tract. These infections are typically mild in nature but can vary in severity. Healthcare providers should be aware of the clinical presentation of _Mycoplasma pneumoniae_ infections, which can manifest with a broad range of symptoms. While many cases are mild, serious complications can occur in some individuals. Risk factors for developing the illness should also be considered. Treatment for _Mycoplasma pneumoniae_ infections may require the use of antibiotics. However, it is important to note that some strains of the bacteria have developed resistance to macrolide antibiotics, which can complicate treatment. For public health professionals, diagnostic testing for _Mycoplasma pneumoniae_ can be performed using various laboratory methods. Detailed guidance is available for submitting specimens to the CDC for testing purposes. Surveillance data on _Mycoplasma pneumoniae_ infections indicate that the exact number of cases occurring annually is not well-documented, highlighting the need for improved monitoring and reporting systems.
